snippet.title: Manali Apple Orchard Farm Food Tour I Manu Temple + Hidimba Temple + Nepali Thakali Food and Momo
snippet.description:
Our last day in Manali unfolded like a slow, comforting melody full of simple pleasures, heartfelt encounters, and flavours that capture the soul of the mountains.

We began the morning at Hotellier, tucking into a basic yet genuinely satisfying breakfast. Nothing extravagant, just honest, comforting food that lifted the spirits as the cold mountain air wrapped around us.

From there, the path led us to the peaceful surroundings of the Hidimba Temple, where towering deodar trees and soft sunlight filtered through like a blessing. The calmness of the shrine set the tone for the day as we walked through its sacred precincts.

A short drive away, the vibes shifted entirely as we entered the bohemian lanes of Old Manali, the cafes, the bustle, the little shops, and the unmistakable charm that travellers always return for. And right in the middle of that cheerful chaos, we met someone unforgettable: a 100-year-old lady selling khumani. Sitting quietly beside her modest display of apricots, she welcomed us with the warmest smile. 

Our next pause was at the German Bakery and Nepali Sandwich Bar, where we picked up a few cookies, sweet, simple bites that kept us going. This was followed by a hearty mealtime stop at Darjeeling Steamers. Their Nepali offerings were truly the highlight: a comforting Nepali thali, flavourful jhol momos, and sesame oil momos that carried the warmth of home-cooked food.

The journey then took us to Mosum Retreat, a hidden haven surrounded by orchards heavy with plums and apples. The sight of trees laden with fruit felt like stepping into nature’s own pantry. Here, we were welcomed by Tarna Devi, who invited us into her world with open arms. In the orchard-side kitchen, she guided us through the making of traditional snacks, childu and giche, each prepared with a simplicity and authenticity that only the hands of experience can offer.

As the day softened into evening light, we accompanied her on a short walk to her village home nearby. The warmth of her hospitality, the stories she shared, and the serene mountain backdrop made it a moment of deep connection, an experience that beautifully tied together our time in Manali.
